title.narrative: COD023N Three Pebbles II (Mawe Tatu II)

description.narrative: Improving the Socio-Economic status of Women and Youth

description.promeva:title: Description (English)
description.narrative: The Mawe Tatu II Consortium (ADJ, COMEN, GEL, CARE DRC, CARE Nederland and ZMQ), will build on its efforts carried out under the previous Mawe Tatu programme: the needs and priorities articulated by the communities we work in, combined with the results of the updated gendered context and problem analysis and its experiences in other programming and proposes focusing on addressing the limited opportunity for Congolese women and youth to exercise their socio-economic rights. The programme will last 36 months and take place in North and South Kivu provinces. It will reach at least 2,500 girls (aged 13-17) and 12,500 women (aged 18-49) organized in VSLAs; 8,000 men (25 years old and above); and 2,500 boys (aged 14-24) organized in Men & Boys Engage reflection groups. Mawe Tatu II’s impact goal is the following: women, men and youth (boys and girls) across North and South Kivu are key actors in - and thus able to contribute to - increased gender equality, promoting and engaging in female-male relations, that can prevent GBV and promote improved household economic management as well as healthier SRH behaviours. The proposed programme has three main Outcomes, focusing on Entrepreneurship (Outcome 1), Engaging Men & Boys to adopt positive masculinities (Outcome 2) and Sexual Reproductive Health Rights (Outcome 3). The programme deploys the following major approaches: the first is CARE’s Village Savings and Loan Association (VSLA) model as an entry point for enterprise development. The second is the “Men & Boys Engage” approach. Advocacy will be structurally embedded in the programme through a jointly elaborated strategic advocacy plan and the programme’s interventions will be adapted, where necessary, based on the results of on in-depth conflict sensitivity analysis foreseen at the start of the programme.
